final_lessons: For this regression dataset, a 3-layer width-256 MLP can beat both shallow models and a deeper width-128 model under low-lr Adam.
For this dataset, balanced 3-layer MLPs are strong; shallow wide models and width-64 residual depth can lag badly.
High width matters strongly here: width-128 deep MLPs can outperform residual models that are only width 32 or 64.
When repeated, the 6-layer width-128 MLP still beats shallow width-256 and very narrow layer-norm networks.
Deep width-128 MLPs, with or without residuals, are the strongest architecture class seen so far; deep width-64 is only middling.
Width-128 residual MLPs remain strong even with layer norm on every layer; width-16/32 models are consistently poor.
Width-64 residual models can be respectable, but known width-128 residual candidates still win by a clear margin.
Deep width-64 non-residual MLPs can be strong enough to beat shallow width-256 models on this dataset.
Repeated candidates confirm 3-layer width-128 is clearly better than shallow width-256 and width-64 residual variants in this setup.
Known 6-layer width-128 candidates remain preferable to shallow width-256 and width-32 options when optimizer, loss, and budget are fixed.
